title: Beaumont Carnegie Library — historic exterior view (date unknown)
caption: Undated exterior view of Beaumont's 1914 Carnegie library at 125 East Eighth Street, showing its original raised entrance, arched windows and stepped parapet framed by cypress trees and clipped hedges.
description: An undated black-and-white view from East Eighth Street records Beaumont's Carnegie library in its original Classical Revival form: a broad stair rises to the central arched entrance, paired pilasters support a curved pediment with a 1914 medallion, and rows of round-arched windows wrap the symmetrical building behind clipped hedges, slender cypress trees and a flagpole. Designed by Los Angeles architect E. L. Hopkins after Beaumont accepted a $10,000 Andrew Carnegie grant in 1913, the building's cornerstone was laid on February 12, 1914, and it opened on June 16 as the first permanent home of the library district created by voters in 1911.
